lines: %1 broke a wrist, and will not hold a blade for a season.
%1 cracked three ribs, and breathes carefully now.
%1 took a fever there that would not lift.
%1 broke a leg, and has to be carried.
%1 took a blow that swelled one eye shut.
%1 wrenched a knee, and walks with a stick.
%1 took a cough from deep in the chest.
%1 took a cut across the hand, and it will not close.
%1 will not talk about %2.
%1 wakes at night from dreams of %2.
%1 faced %2, and it cost something.
%1 went quiet at the first sight of %2, and has stayed quiet.
%1 sleeps with a lamp lit now. It was %2.
%1 did not come home from %2.
%1 lies at %2 now.
%2 kept %1.
They carried %1 home from %2 under a cloak.
%1 learned from it.
%1 came back knowing more than went out.
%1 watched the others closely, and it shows.
%1 saw how it was done, and will do it again.
died in the night, in the first hard frost
did not come down to breakfast one morning in midwinter
sat down by the fire after supper and did not get up again
died at midwinter, with the house asleep
went out to look at the snow, came in, and died before the fire was lit
died in bed at the turn of the year, with the window open
fell asleep over a book in the last week of winter
died on the longest night, and was found smiling
SLEEP_DEATHS._note: Used verbatim as a fate telling (a predicate phrase, no subject).

lines: A child was born to %1 and %2 in the last week of winter.
%1 and %2 have a child, born on a night of heavy snow.
The midwife was sent for at dusk. By morning %1 and %2 had a child.
A child for %1 and %2, born at the thaw.
%1 came up the road with the first thaw and asked for a place at the fire.
%1 had heard of the house three valleys away, and walked.
%1 arrived with one bag and a letter nobody could read, and was let in.
%1 came to the door in the rain and has not been asked to leave.
%1 and %2 were wed at midwinter. The whole house stood witness.
%1 and %2 were wed by the hearth, with snow at the windows.
%1 and %2 walked in the garden until it was decided. They are wed.
%1 told the tale at the long table. People will repeat it.
%1 told it plainly, and the hall was silent to the end.
%1 told the tale three nights running, and it grew a little each night.
%1 rested by the fire.
%1 slept late and mended.
%1 kept to the hearth all winter.
%1 stood in front of %2 and did not run
%1 looked at %2 for a long moment, and then went on
%1 walked into %2 with both hands shaking, and walked out again
%1 went first, into %2, without being asked
COURAGES._note: A sentence fragment without a full stop; see lines.json fear.courage.

lines: %1 and %2 talked the whole road home. They are friends.
%1 and %2 have been through two good days together now. They are friends.
%1 carried the pack of %2 the last ten miles, and was let. They are friends.
%1 and %2 finish each other's stories already. They are friends.
